title: Cross-cycle stitching guidelines and initiative rhythm for hosted API + model catalog
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Establish repeatable guidance that ties quarterly roadmap commitments for the Hosted API surface to the model catalog lifecycle. Deliver a lightweight pattern for stitching initiatives across cycles (handoff, canary windows, contingency lanes, and decision triggers) to reduce churn between PM, Eng, and Infra during model rotation and endpoint releases.
background: We repeatedly see friction at the boundary between quarterly planning and execution: model onboarding timelines slip because hosted API integration work is not scheduled, and dedicated capacity forecasts diverge from catalog commitments. Current artifacts are ad-hoc sprint notes and post-hoc incident threads. This ticket captures a formalized cross-cycle stitching pattern so teams can predict lift, reserve capacity, and set explicit rollback/contingency triggers.
objectives: Define a 6-step cross-cycle handoff checklist for model->endpoint->ops
Create a cadence and artifacts that map OKRs/initiatives to canary windows and capacity hedges
Reduce unplanned model swaps during a cycle by 50% (measured by swap-related incidents)
Provide PM/Eng guardrails to make scope trade-offs explicit at commit time
scope: Produce the guideline doc, a reusable Linear template for cross-cycle initiative cards, recommended gating checklist, and example calendar for a three-cycle sequence. Pilot with two upcoming Hosted API + model catalog initiatives.
out_of_scope: Automating routing or infra-level capacity allocation; detailed scheduling of Dedicated pools (this will be a follow-up with Infra team).
acceptance_criteria: Guideline doc reviewed and approved by Eng, Runtime, and Console PMs
Linear template created and used for at least two pilot initiatives
Canary and rollback triggers defined and validated in tabletop run with SREs
Stakeholder sign-offs captured in the doc and linked PRs
tasks: Work with SRE to enumerate canary metrics and rollback thresholds
Create Linear template and pre-filled sample for upcoming Initiative A and Initiative B
Run 30-minute tabletop with Runtime, Infra, SRE, and Growth to validate triggers
Publish guidelines to Confluence and add links to roadmap cadence calendar
timeline: Feb 2025: draft -> Feb 2–9 reviews -> Feb 10 tabletop -> Feb 17 pilot templates created -> Mar 1 publish and run pilot
risks: Teams bypass template and continue ad-hoc coordination (mitigate via required sign-off in planning ritual)
Insufficient capacity forecasts from Infra causing committed canary windows to be infeasible (mitigate with early capacity sync)
Ambiguous ownership of rollback decisions leading to delayed action
tradeoffs: Prescriptive cadence vs. flexibility: proposed pattern is intentionally lightweight (one checklist + calendar) to avoid over-burdening small initiatives
Conservative canaries reduce customer exposure but increase rollout time; the guideline favors short, automated canaries with strict metrics to balance safety and speed
Locking model catalog commit windows improves predictability but may delay rapid model improvements for high-priority customers
decisions: Adopt a 3-week pre-commit runway: all model-onboarding tasks must be visible 3 weeks before committed release week
Require SRE sign-off for any canary that spans multiple regions
Use token-cost and latency counters plus error-rate for primary canary metrics
notes: Pilot candidates: Q2 image-captioning hosted endpoint (expected model swap), and search-rerank model rotation for enterprise tier
Reference: recent swap incident (postmortem link) highlighted unclear rollback ownership
Plan to incorporate Runtime Optimize suggestions as prescriptive pre-commit checks in a follow-up
metrics: Average latency delta during canaries (target: < 5% above baseline)
Time between commit and rollback decision (target: < 30 minutes during canary)
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Publish guideline and Linear template. Stage 2: Apply template to two pilot initiatives and run tabletop. Stage 3: Iterate on checklist and embed sign-off step into sprint planning. Stage 4: Measure swap incidents over two quarters and recommend org-level cadence changes.
